role.altitude: The career and technical teacher keeps teaching remedial sessions, preparing the workshop, meeting colleagues about students, supervising projects and trips and guiding reflection; compiling score exports, copying marks into meeting notes, mailing agreements, rebuilding evidence of preparation and chasing paper slips shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted worksheets against the lesson goal
Working from student overviews in the pupil system
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose time goes to the workshop and the students who need extra help.

tasks.short: Compile marks for students requiring extra help, decide who needs it, write remedial plans, prepare materials, run remedial sessions, inform parents and record progress.

steps.what: Teacher exports marks per learning goal into a spreadsheet
Teacher decides which students require extra help
Teacher writes the remedial programs per student or group
Teacher prepares remedial exercises and materials
Teacher implements remedial sessions with students
Teacher informs parents about the remedial plan
Teacher records student progress

tasks.design: A view in the pupil system lists students below the agreed level per learning goal, instead of the teacher exporting marks into a spreadsheet. A remedial plan template takes the student's goals from the system, and the teacher writes the approach. Where the subject has adaptive practice, exercises are assigned per learning goal. Choosing students, running sessions and informing parents stay with the teacher. No software decides who gets help.
tasks.previous_blocker: Marks were exported into spreadsheets to find who needed help.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning-goal views in the pupil system and plan templates.
tasks.still_hard: Practical skills that marks do not capture.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a student's problem is confidence, not skill.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil system holds pupil records, a support plan module and learning-goal tracking.
An adaptive practice tool drafts a class activity for a lesson goal.

assumptions: Boundary: remedial programs; adapting methods and materials (task 6615) and maintaining student records (task 6611) are sibling tasks.
s7 is part of maintaining student records, which sibling task 6611 covers; its saving is counted there.
s1 saves exporting and sorting marks; deciding stays in s2.
Sessions and parent contact keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of practical subjects with adaptive practice.
research_questions: Does remedial help start earlier in the term?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: practical subjects without goal tracking or adaptive practice, so s1 keeps 70 and s4 keeps 100 (3.6); high: subjects with goal tracking and adaptive practice (5.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather marks, absence and notes, meet with other professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress, write notes and agreements, mail them and follow up.

steps.what: Teacher copies marks, absence and notes on the student into a meeting note
Teacher meets with other professionals to discuss the student's needs and progress
Teacher writes the meeting notes and agreements
Teacher checks the actions before they notify colleagues: each agreement, owner and date as agreed in the meeting
Teacher sends the checked agreements to the colleagues involved: by mail today, as action notifications from the student file after the change
Teacher follows up on the agreements

tasks.design: A student overview in the pupil system shows marks, absence, notes and the support plan on one screen, instead of the teacher copying them into a meeting note. Meeting notes use a template in the student file. Agreements are entered as actions with owner and date; the teacher checks them and releases them once as notifications to the colleagues involved, instead of a separate mail. Meeting, deciding and following up stay with the teacher. Only staff involved with the student can see the notes.

approvals.approved_version: The actions with each agreement, owner and date exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once as notifications to the colleagues named as owners; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Information was copied from several screens and agreements were mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Student overviews and actions in the pupil system.
tasks.still_hard: Students supported by outside agencies with their own files.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which colleague a student trusts.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and mailing; the meeting stays.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil system holds pupil records, a support plan module and learning-goal tracking.
Parents and pupils have a say in rules for pupil data through the school's participation council.

assumptions: Boundary: meetings with other professionals; meetings with parents (task 6625) and counselling students (task 6623) are sibling tasks.

s1 saves copying data already in the pupil system; s4 saves mailing agreements already entered as actions and keeps 30 for the release; the check before it keeps its full time. Meeting notes are a first record: s3 keeps 90, saving only the layout.
Support needs are health data; access is limited to staff involved, and a DPIA is done.
Meeting and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of student meetings per month.
research_questions: Are agreements followed up on time more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many students have files outside the pupil system and colleagues still want a mail, so s1 keeps 80 and s4 keeps 70 (4.4); high: students fully in the pupil system (9.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the week's classes, prepare materials and the workshop, write lesson plans, show written evidence of preparation upon request, discuss with colleagues and track materials needed.

steps.what: Teacher reviews the week's assigned classes and the curriculum plan
Teacher prepares worksheets, explanations and demonstrations for practical lessons

loop.input: The teacher's lesson goal, outline and the section's material library.
loop.output: A draft worksheet or explanation at the class's level.
loop.check: The teacher reads every draft, checks safety instructions for tools and machines, and edits before use.
loop.stop: The teacher writes the material when two drafts miss the goal.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each class and practical task needs its own wording.

steps.what: Teacher prepares the workshop: tools, materials and machines
Teacher writes lesson plans in a personal planner
Teacher compiles written evidence of preparation when the supervisor asks
Supervisor reviews the preparation
Teacher discusses preparation with colleagues
Teacher tracks the materials needed per lesson in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: A drafting step writes worksheets and explanations from the teacher's lesson goal and outline and the section's material library. The teacher checks every draft, including safety instructions for tools and machines. Lesson plans use a short template in the section's shared space linked to the series outline, so evidence of preparation is a link, not a new document. Preparing the workshop, discussing with colleagues and the supervisor's review stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials and plans were written from scratch and evidence compiled on request.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from the teacher's outline and shared plan templates.
tasks.still_hard: Practical demonstrations that only work at the machine.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which machine step a class will get wrong.
tasks.altitude: Less writing from scratch; workshop preparation stays.

reach.learn: Whether plans are available without asking.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial with 259 science teachers, a chatbot with a guide cut weekly planning time by 31% with no quality difference.
In a randomised trial with 464 primary teachers, an AI lesson assistant cut preparation by 24%, but it covered 7% of lessons and use declined.
Staff consent through the participation council is needed for tools that can monitor them.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing classes and showing evidence; instructing students (task 6610) and selecting and ordering equipment and supplies (task 20241) are sibling tasks.
s8 is part of selecting, storing and ordering materials, which sibling task 20241 covers; its saving is counted there.
s2 is priced at 80 because the trials found 24-31% less planning time but low and declining use; practical subjects use fewer worksheets.
Supervisor time is shown in s6 and is outside the teacher's savings; using shared plans for appraisal needs staff consent.
unknowns: Share of preparation that is written material.
research_questions: Does preparation time fall without lower lesson quality?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks and edits drafted materials.

incremental.description: Teacher adds checked materials to the section library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: as in the trials, drafts are used little and plans stay in the personal planner, so s2 keeps 95 and s4 keeps 90 (5.4); high: drafts and shared plans used as designed (11.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose and plan the project, field trip or guest speaker, get approval, book, write and check the parent form, send it, collect consent and payments, supervise the activity and guide students in learning from it.

steps.what: Teacher chooses the class project, field trip or guest speaker and its learning goals
Teacher writes the plan and risk assessment for field trips and visits
School leader approves the activity, cost and supervision ratio
Teacher prepares the booking requests for transport, venue or guest speaker: by phone and e-mail today, from standard request texts after the change
Teacher checks each booking request before it goes: provider, date, times, number of students and cost against the approved plan
Teacher sends the checked booking requests to the providers
Teacher writes the parent letter and consent slip with date, cost and medical questions
Teacher checks the final parent form against the approved plan
Teacher sends the trip letter and form to parents
Parents give consent, medical notes and payment for field trips
Teacher collects paper consent slips, medical notes and payments from parents
Teacher supervises students during the project, trip or visit
Teacher guides students in learning from the activity

approvals.approved_version: The parent form with date, cost, consent text and medical questions exactly as checked by the teacher in s6 against the plan approved in s3, sent to the parents of the students on the activity list; any change needs a new check before sending.

Each booking request with provider, date, times, number of students and cost exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b against the plan the school leader approved in s3, sent once to that provider; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: A plan template carries the school's standard risks, supervision ratios and checklist. Bookings use standard request texts within the plan the school leader approved. The approved plan fills a parent form with date, cost, consent text and medical questions. The teacher checks it and sends it through the parent app of the pupil system. Parents answer and pay in the app, and a live list shows who has responded; paper slips stay for parents without the app. Choosing the activity, supervising and guiding learning stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were written from scratch and consent slips and cash collected on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Plan templates and parent app forms with payment.
tasks.still_hard: Parents who do not use the app.
tasks.human_edge: Turning a company visit into a lesson students remember.
tasks.altitude: Less paper chasing; the activity stays.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil system includes a parent app.

assumptions: Boundary: from choosing the activity to guiding learning; school-wide events are outside.
Input contract for s9: about 70% of parents use the parent app; s9 is priced at that share.
s7 saves printing and handing out letters for parents who use the app.
Parents' time is shown in s8 at share 1 and is about what the paper slip took.
School leader and parent time is outside the teacher's savings.
Supervision and guiding learning do not change.
s2 keeps 70 because the teacher still writes the activity-specific plan and risks; the template fills the standard ones.
unknowns: Number of trips and visits per year.
research_questions: Do fewer students miss trips for missing slips?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks the response list and contacts missing parents.

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; setting up the form is part of writing it in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about a third of parents use the app, so letters are still printed (s7 at 80) and slips and cash collected (s9 at 70) (7.6); high: about 70% of parents use the app as assumed (10.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
